text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.

WHEAT SALE - Giant U.S. grain trader Cargill Inc reached an agreement with the government of North Korea on Saturday to sell them an undisclosed amount of U.S. wheat, marking its first commercial sale of American grain to the communist regime. Cargill would not comment on the amount of the wheat but the U.s. government the first of the year first gave the exporter approval to sell 500,000 tonnes of wheat and/or rice to the country. Cargill also said it was hopeful that the deal just concluded will lead to more grain sales to that country.

BARLEY TENDER - British barley could be used to supply some of the 500,000 tonnes Saudi Arabia is seeking under its latest tender, UK traders said. Saudia Arabia has launched an April 8 tender for 500,000 tonnes of barley of optional origin for delivery in a range of delivery periods ranging from the second half April to the second half of May, European grain traders said on Monday.
- The South African Wheat Board said it was offering 25,150 tonnes of feed grade barley for export sale no later than April 30.

CORN AND WHEAT TENDER - The Cyprus Grain Commission last week invited tenders for the supply of an combined shipment of 10,000 tonnes spring and 8,000 tonnes durum wheat, and a shipment of 18,000 tonnes of corn. Shipment for the combined wheat cargo is scheduled at the end of April or the beginning of May, while the corn shipment is scheduled the beginning of May 1997. Both tenders close on April 8.
SOYBEAN TENDER - Exporters said they changed a 108,000-tonne sale of U.S. soybeans to Taiwan for 1996/97 delivery to optional origin, USDA said.
RICE TENDER - Syria seeks 12,000 tonnes of white rice for shipment between April 20 and May 20. April 8 is the final date for bids and result will be announced on April 16.

MARKET TALK - The Canadian Wheat Board on Monday declined comment on rumors it sold between 0.5 million and 1.5 million tonnes of wheat to China for June-July delivery. "We neither confirm nor deny there was any sale," the CWB said.
Trade rumors had the United States selling a cargo load of wheat to China and Canada selling 0.5 to 1.5 million tonnes to China for June-July delivery.

... South Korean feed milling firms and Japanese vegetable oil makers are seen buying soymeal for June delivery, but other East Asian buyers are seen sitting back due to volatile Chicago futures prices, traders said on Monday.

... The Korea Feed Association is expected to seek 50,000 tonnes of soymeal while Big Feed Mills is likely to pick up 20,000 to 30,000 tonnes of tapioca for June shipment this week, a local trader said.
... France has agreed to grant Bulgaria 5,000 tonnes of wheat to alleviate shortages, state news agency BTA said.
... A vessel carrying 52,000 tonnes of French wheat purchased under Iraq's oil-for-food deal with the United Nations will discharge at Jordan's Red Sea port of Aqaba in mid-month, shippers said.
